newsitem.title: GERMANY: Young CDU leader urges German EMU flexibility.
newsitem.headline: Young CDU leader urges German EMU flexibility.

text.p: An up-and-coming young leader of Chancellor Helmut Kohl's Christian Democratic Union (CDU) urged the cash-strapped German government on Friday to interpret the Maastricht treaty's deficit criteria more flexibly.

Peter Mueller, CDU leader in Saar state, said Bonn's controversial plan to revalue Bundesbank gold and currency reserves to meet the Maastricht deficit target to the letter gave the impression of nervousness.
Mueller, one of the CDU's leading younger politicians, told German Radio: "I think we should talk again about which deficit criteria the Maastricht treaty provides for.
"This is the source of the problem. We have manoeuvered ourselves into a situation that the treaty does not require.
"A reasonable look at the Maastricht treaty shows there is no obligation to have a deficit of 3.0 percent. There is room to manoeuvre and we should use it."

Finance Minister Theo Waigel, who opted for the gold plan to help fill yawning gaps in his 1997 budget without going over the three percent deficit-to-GDP target, has long insisted only a strict interpretation of the Maastricht criteria would ensure that Europe's monetary union (EMU) is stable.
